definitions.explanation: To dispatch or transmit something to someone else. Used for letters, packages, emails, etc.
To accompany someone who is leaving, or to escort them partway.

examples.japanese: ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→てがみ：00675⟧⟦を→を：00422⟧{送|おく}りました。

examples.english: I'll send a letter to my mother.

examples.japanese: ⟦{荷物|にもつ}→にもつ：00737⟧⟦を→を：00422⟧{送|おく}って⟦ください→ください：02899⟧。
⟦{友達|ともだち}→ともだち：01478⟧⟦に→に：00314⟧⟦{写真|しゃしん}→しゃしん：00753⟧⟦を→を：00422⟧{送|おく}りました。
examples.english: I sent photos to my friend.
I'm thinking of sending a letter to my mother. I want to ask if she's doing well.
I'll walk you to the station.
Shall I give you a ride?

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→こども：00554⟧⟦を→を：00422⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→がっこう：00055⟧⟦まで→まで：00490⟧{送|おく}ってあげます。
examples.english: I'll take the child to school.
Every morning I drop the kids off at school and then go to work. My wife picks them up on the way home.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb. Pattern: XをYに{送|おく}る (send X to Y) or Xを{送|おく}る (see X off).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action or completed action depending on context. {送|おく}っている = 'is sending' or 'has sent.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・⟦{手紙|てがみ}→てがみ：00675⟧を{送|おく}る (send a letter)
・⟦メール→めーる：04435⟧を{送|おく}る (send an email)
・⟦{荷物|にもつ}→にもつ：00737⟧を{送|おく}る (send a package)
・⟦{駅|えき}→えき：02180⟧まで{送|おく}る (walk someone to the station)

Related:
- {送|おく}り{迎|むか}え (pick-up and drop-off)
- ⟦{見送|みおく}る→みおくる：04240⟧ (to see off).
